verdict: Caution: lend selectively to component and tooling suppliers tied to anchor OEMs, with tight monthly discipline; avoid thin-margin pure assembly units and any borrower whose GST filings lag the state trend.
title: Sriperumbudur mobile & consumer-electronics assembly: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
**This is a screwdriver-and-test-line business: imported kits, boards and displays go in, finished handsets come out, and the cash is made on throughput, not on price.** The assembler earns a conversion fee per unit from the brand owner; the brand owns the design, the bill of materials and the pricing. So when a proposal lands, check who the customer is and whether the contract is a fixed conversion rate or a cost-plus arrangement; if it is cost-plus, ask what happens to the rate when the PLI-linked incentive ends [5].

**Value sits with the brand and the component maker, not the assembler.** Peer commentary is blunt that Indian electronics makers remain stuck in assembly mode with razor-thin margins [6], and Dixon's Q2FY27 topline beat came with sub-par operating performance as input costs rose and PLI support ended [5]. So when a proposal lands, check the gross-margin trend over four quarters; if margins are flat while revenue doubles, ask where the working-capital funding is coming from.

## Where the cash actually sits
**Cash is trapped in inventory and receivables, and the cycle is set by the brand, not the borrower.** Components are imported on LC or advance, while the brand pays 45-90 days after dispatch. So when a proposal lands, check the inventory days and receivable days separately; if receivable days exceed the brand's stated credit terms, ask for the ageing and the debit notes. Capex is modest per line but recurring, because each new model needs new jigs and testers; collect from customer the per-line capex and the model-change frequency.

## What has changed now
**The national picture is strong and the state picture is not.** India-wide electronics output (IIP NIC 26) is up 19.3% YoY and 13.6% Apr-to-date, and exports are up 44.0% Apr-to-date in USD [D]. But Tamil Nadu GST collections are down 3.2% Apr-to-date against India's +6.1%, a 9.3 pp gap [D]. **That gap is the single most important number in this note.** So when a proposal lands, pull the borrower's own GST returns; if its filings are shrinking faster than the state, ask why before sanctioning.

**Local reporting on Sriperumbudur itself is thin.** The local coverage is topic-page aggregation rather than plant-level news [1][3], and the China+1 piece is a policy essay, not a Sriperumbudur datapoint [2]. Treat first principles and peer results as the base, and verify plant-level facts on the ground.

## Who to pursue, and how to grow safely
**Pursue the second tier: tooling and jig makers, precision plastics, packaging, SMT job-workers and logistics/warehouse operators serving the anchor plants.** These have diversified customers, shorter receivable cycles and real asset backing. Avoid pure assembly units with a single brand customer and no component capability. Structure term loans against machinery with a 25-30% margin, working capital as CC/OD against stock and book debts with a drawing power reset monthly, and take a monthly stock statement, monthly GST return, and quarterly customer-wise sales. Covenant a maximum single-customer share and a minimum current ratio; if the single-customer share crosses the covenant, ask for a customer diversification plan before enhancing limits.

## Early-warning signs
- **GST filings falling faster than the state's -3.2% [D] (monthly)** -> freeze enhancement and inspect stock.
- **Receivable days stretching beyond the brand's stated terms (monthly)** -> ask for the brand's payment confirmation in writing.
- **Inventory days rising while dispatches fall (monthly)** -> check for obsolete model stock and revalue drawing power.
- **Conversion rate cut or model discontinued (event-driven)** -> reassess the line's utilisation and the loan tenor.
- **Power or labour disruption at the anchor plant (weekly)** -> confirm the borrower's order book is not single-plant dependent.
